source.paper: ByT5-Sanskrit: Sentence-Level Pretraining Outperforms Token-Level Pretraining for Sanskrit NLP
source.authors: Sebastian Nehrdich, Oliver Hellwig, Kurt Keutzer

correction_to_handoff_premise.handoff_claimed: its DCS table reports 90.11 / 93.83 / 94.29 on three tagging metrics
correction_to_handoff_premise.actual: 90.11 / 93.83 / 94.29 are Table 3 sentence-level perfect matches on three WORD SEGMENTATION datasets (DCS 2018 / SIGHUM / Hackathon), not tagging metrics.
correction_to_handoff_premise.table_3_caption: Table 3: Sentence level perfect matches on previous Sanskrit word segmentation tasks.
correction_to_handoff_premise.consequence: No published ByT5-Sanskrit token-level UPOS/FEATS/lemma tagging number exists to compare against. The paper's only morphosyntax-bearing figures are sentence-level perfect matches of JOINT tasks (Table 7).

metric: sentence-level perfect match (whole sentence reproduced exactly), not token-level accuracy
comparability_note: Arm A is a sequence-level perfect-match figure over joint segmentation+lemmatisation+tagging on the paper's own April-2024 DCS split (dev 8,190 / test 8,398 sentences). Arm B, as specified by H7248, is token-level UPOS/FEATS/lemma accuracy on a freshly frozen stratified sample. The two are not the same metric and not the same split: every Arm A number below is split- AND metric-adjusted and must not be tabulated beside Arm B token accuracies without that label.

table_7_dcs_joint_tasks_sentence_perfect.note: S = segmentation, L = lemmatisation, M = morphosyntax tagging. No row isolates M alone: every M figure is contaminated by segmentation and/or lemmatisation decisions, and all are sentence-level perfect matches.

split.test_bias: test and validation splits contain no heuristically reconstructed forms and are therefore strongly biased towards Vedic texts (paper §5.5)
